clue.text: Christians anticipate this moment before Advent

blocks.note: a very brief instant of time
an advent is an arrival

explanation.surface: A seasonal note that the faithful await something in the run-up to Advent in the church calendar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' sets one piece ahead of the other, and 'Advent' with its capital looks like the church season but is just an arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian doctrine holds that Christ will return to Earth at the end of time, an event believers await.

clue.text: Frighten Les, spilling acid in the process

indicators.note: spilling suggests letters tumbling out of place and landing in a new order
something put in the process goes into the middle of whatever is being worked on

blocks.note: taken as written
tart means sour or acidic

explanation.surface: Someone startles Les by knocking acid over during a laboratory experiment.
explanation.walkthrough: Les is rearranged as SLE, and TART is slipped between its first letter and the rest to give STARTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To startle someone is to give them a sudden shock or fright, a close synonym.

clue.text: Skill of flying men shown in court

indicators.note: being shown in somewhere means standing inside it, so one group sits within another

blocks.note: the Royal Air Force, Britain's air arm
standard abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: Airmen are brought before a court, perhaps showing off their flying ability.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying men' is a crossword stock phrase for Britain's Royal Air Force; 'shown in' places them inside the court abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Craft means skill or expertise in making or doing something, as in a potter's craft.

clue.text: Tidiest home to have a meal in

indicators.note: a place that is to have something in it will hold it within its walls

blocks.note: a nest is a bird's home, and a cosy home generally
to have a meal is to eat

explanation.surface: Praise for the most orderly house to dine in.
explanation.walkthrough: The home here is a bird's, and having a meal is simply the verb, sitting inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat means tidy and orderly, so its superlative form matches the superlative of tidy.

clue.text: See 1
Nothing changes with egg producers

blocks.note: zero, shaped like the letter O
to change is to vary

explanation.surface: A shrug that hens and other layers never alter their habits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changes' looks like an anagram signal but is simply a synonym supplying the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovaries are the female organs in which egg cells are formed and released.

clue.text: It's even in liquid that's concentrated

indicators.note: something liquid flows and has no fixed shape, so these letters can be poured into a new form

blocks.note: the letters as printed, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Remarks that a dissolved solution is evenly spread and strong.
explanation.definitionFit: Intensive effort or study is focused and concentrated in a short period or narrow area.

clue.text: Feeling George will take work home by midnight

blocks.note: GR, Georgius Rex, is King George's royal cipher
an opus, a piece of work
at home means in
the middle of night, read literally

explanation.surface: George is bringing his work home and staying up until midnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Midnight' is a crossword favourite: read as mid-night it is the central letter of night, not a time.
explanation.definitionFit: Groping is fumbling about by touch, searching with the hands in the dark.

clue.text: Backing places without first aid is silly

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word is read from its end
without its first means the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: to place is to put
taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that withdrawing first-aid posts is a foolish policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First aid' reads as a phrase, but 'first' belongs to the deletion signal: aid loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupid and silly both describe behaviour lacking sense or good judgement.

clue.text: Film obese gangster with charm

blocks.note: obese means very fat
Al Capone, the archetypal Chicago gangster
charm is a quality that attracts

explanation.surface: Describes a movie about a portly mobster with a winning personality.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatal Attraction is the 1987 thriller starring Michael Douglas and Glenn Close.

clue.text: Susan's taken round thanks to model figure

indicators.note: to be taken round something is to wrap about it, enclosing it

blocks.note: Sue is a short form of Susan
ta is informal British for thank you
the Model T, Henry Ford's car

explanation.surface: Susan has been shown round, with gratitude, by a fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model figure' looks like one phrase but splits: model is the Ford Model T and figure is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a sculpted figure of a person or animal, carved or cast in stone or metal.

clue.text: I grope in jumble for a dressinggown

indicators.note: a jumble is a disordered heap, so these letters are muddled together

blocks.note: the letters as printed

explanation.surface: Someone rummages through a jumble sale hunting for a bathrobe.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumble sale is a British charity sale of second-hand goods, which suits the rummaging picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A peignoir is a light, loose woman's robe or négligée worn over nightwear, a kind of dressing gown.

clue.text: Character caught in the act left

indicators.note: something caught in another thing is trapped inside it

blocks.note: an actor's character is the part played
a deed is an act

explanation.surface: A rogue is caught red-handed and the villain then runs off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught in the act' is a stock phrase, but it splits: the act is the outer word and 'left' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Departed is the past tense of depart, meaning went away, exactly as left does.

clue.text: Is, for example, standing in canal - possibly to relieve pain

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective (or noun) for something that relieves pain

indicators.note: standing in a place means being within it, so these words go inside
possibly marks one possible rearrangement rather than the given order

blocks.note: taken as written
e.g., exempli gratia
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether wading into a canal might ease their aches.
explanation.walkthrough: IS and EG go into CANAL, and the whole lot is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An analgesic drug or effect acts as a painkiller, easing discomfort without loss of consciousness.

clue.text: Mean to take for a ride before the end of July

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: to sting is to swindle or con
the final letter of the month

explanation.surface: Someone plans to give a person a lift just before July is out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like a verb meaning intend; it is the adjective for tight-fisted.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingy and mean both describe someone reluctant to spend or give money.

clue.text: Eccentric suppresses cry of pain, but he's scared

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold something down and keep it inside

blocks.note: a card is an eccentric or amusing character
an exclamation of pain

explanation.surface: An oddball stifles a yelp, though inwardly he is terrified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' looks like an anagram signal; here it means an oddball, a card.
explanation.definitionFit: A coward is a person lacking courage, one who is easily frightened.

clue.text: They speak of nothing to a fellow painting hills

blocks.note: zero
a Royal Academician, a fellow of the Royal Academy of Arts
tors are rocky hilltops, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: People chat idly to a landscape artist at work on a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Painting' describes the fellow: an artist elected to the Royal Academy is an RA.
explanation.definitionFit: Orators are public speakers, people who deliver formal speeches.

clue.text: I dig right out, getting free

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so these pieces are not in their proper places

blocks.note: taken as written
to delve is to dig
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A prisoner tunnels his way out to escape.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver someone is to set them free or rescue them, as in 'deliver us from evil'.

clue.text: Came clean: he'd worse troubles

indicators.note: troubles here is a verb: to trouble is to disturb, throwing things into disorder

blocks.note: the letters as printed, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A man confessed, admitting he'd had worse difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Came clean' suggests confessing; read literally, it means got washed.
explanation.definitionFit: To shower is to wash under running water, so someone who showered literally came out clean.

clue.text: Governing body wants Brown back in the diocese

indicators.note: back means going in the opposite direction, so the word reads in reverse
in places one word inside another

blocks.note: tan is a light brown
a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: A church council wants a man called Brown to return to its diocese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' with its capital looks like a surname; it is just the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A senate is a legislative or governing assembly, as in Rome or the US Congress.

clue.text: Scrap outmoded books

indicators.note: out means wrong or awry, so the letters attached to it are disordered

blocks.note: the word after its opening signal, whose letters are to be rearranged
the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: An instruction to throw away old-fashioned books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outmoded' must be split in two: 'out' is the signal and 'moded' the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddment is a leftover scrap or remnant, such as a piece of fabric left from a roll.

clue.text: Distinguished crossword compiler standing in hospital department

indicators.note: standing in a place is being set within it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: the setter refers to himself as me
taken as written
ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A celebrated setter is found standing about in a ward.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often call themselves 'me'; here 'in' sits inside that, and the pair stand within the ear, nose and throat department.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent describes someone famous and respected in their field, a close synonym.

clue.text: Pop in, carrying unusually long mammal

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside another
unusually means not in the normal way, so the word's letters are reordered

blocks.note: pop and pa both mean father
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An invitation to drop by, bringing along a strangely elongated animal.
explanation.walkthrough: PA and IN together surround the rearranged LONG.
explanation.definitionFit: The pangolin is a scaly anteater of Africa and Asia, a mammal covered in protective plates.

clue.text: Wreckage in sea beside Bristol

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: spans the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Flotsam bobs in the Bristol Channel near the port.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is scattered fragments of something wrecked or destroyed.

clue.text: Live humdrum existence assumed to be without intelligence

indicators.note: to assume something is to take it on, so one word takes another inside it

blocks.note: to be is to exist, to live
a rut is a dull, unchanging routine

explanation.surface: A dreary life is taken to show a lack of brains.
explanation.definitionFit: Brute as an adjective means lacking reason or understanding, as in brute force or a brute beast.

clue.text: Part of theatre greeting first lady of song

blocks.note: the gods are the highest gallery seats in a theatre
ave is Latin for hail
the monarch is the first lady of the land

explanation.surface: The gallery hails a celebrated female singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First lady of song' reads as a diva's title, but 'song' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: God Save the Queen was the British national anthem, a patriotic song sung at state occasions.

clue.text: Obtain safe

blocks.note: first meaning: to get hold of or acquire
second meaning: protected from danger

explanation.walkthrough: 'Safe' looks like a noun, a strongbox; it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb for acquiring something and as an adjective for being out of danger.

clue.text: Certify a tin-opener on trial

indicators.note: an opener is what comes first, so only the initial letter is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter
a trial is a test

explanation.surface: Someone vouches for a can opener being put through its paces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tin-opener' looks like a kitchen gadget; it means the opening letter of tin.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to declare or certify formally that something is true or genuine.
